skills.name: setup_incidence_correspondence
skills.description: Construct an incidence variety that records tuples of geometric objects satisfying prescribed incidence or tangency conditions.
skills.preconditions: A family of objects parameterized by a scheme and a list of algebraic conditions relating them.
skills.postconditions: A new scheme equipped with projection maps to the original parameter spaces, encoding the incidence data.
skills.example: For lines in the projective plane, define the incidence variety of pairs (ℓ, p) such that the line ℓ passes through the point p; the variety sits inside the product of the Grassmannian of lines and the plane and projects to each factor.

skills.name: compute_chow_class_of_incidence
skills.description: Determine the class of an incidence subvariety in the Chow ring of the ambient product space using the defining equations.
skills.preconditions: An incidence subvariety defined by explicit homogeneous equations inside a product of projective varieties.
skills.postconditions: An explicit expression for the cycle class of the incidence subvariety in terms of the standard generators of the Chow ring.
skills.example: The class of the incidence of a line meeting a fixed point in \(\mathbb{P}^2\) is the product of the hyperplane class from the Grassmannian and the point class from the plane.

skills.name: apply_projection_formula
skills.description: Use the projection formula to relate the push‑forward of an intersection product on a product space to intersection products on the target space.
skills.preconditions: A proper morphism between varieties and a product of cycles on the source that includes a pull‑back from the target.
skills.postconditions: An equality expressing the push‑forward of the product as the product of the push‑forward of one factor with the other factor on the target.
skills.example: If \(π:\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^2\to\mathbb{P}^2\) is the projection, then \(π_*(π^*H\cdot D)=H\cdot π_*D\), where \(H\) is the hyperplane class on \(\mathbb{P}^2\).

skills.name: use_finite_etale_morphism_fiber_average
skills.description: Compute the average size of fibers of a finite étale morphism by recognizing that the average equals the degree of the morphism.
skills.preconditions: A finite étale morphism between varieties defined over a finite field and a large enough set of rational points on the base where the morphism is étale.
skills.postconditions: The average cardinality of fibers over the chosen rational points is equal to the degree of the morphism.
skills.example: For the map \(f:\mathbb{A}^1\to\mathbb{A}^1\) given by \(x\mapsto x^2-1\) over \(\mathbb{F}_p\) (with \(p\) odd), the morphism is étale away from the branch points, and the average number of preimages of a point in the étale locus equals the degree two.

skills.name: apply_lang_weil_to_count_points
skills.description: Estimate the number of \(\mathbb{F}_q\)-rational points on a geometrically irreducible variety using Lang–Weil bounds.
skills.preconditions: A geometrically irreducible projective variety of known dimension defined over a finite field.
skills.postconditions: An asymptotic formula \(\#X(\mathbb{F}_q)=q^{\dim X}+O(q^{\dim X-1/2})\) giving the leading term and error bound.
skills.example: A smooth plane cubic curve over \(\mathbb{F}_q\) has \(q+1+O(\sqrt{q})\) rational points by Lang–Weil.

skills.name: deduce_degree_from_generic_fiber_cardinality
skills.description: Infer the degree of a dominant morphism by counting points in a generic fiber over an algebraically closed field.
skills.preconditions: A dominant morphism between varieties where the generic fiber is finite and reduced.
skills.postconditions: The degree of the morphism equals the number of points in the generic fiber, counted with multiplicity one.
skills.example: The projection from a smooth quadric surface in \(\mathbb{P}^3\) onto a plane is dominant; a generic line in the plane meets the quadric in two points, so the projection has degree two.

skills.name: use_galois_action_to_split_fiber_components
skills.description: Analyze the decomposition of a fiber into geometrically irreducible components by studying the action of the absolute Galois group on its points.
skills.preconditions: A finite morphism defined over a non‑algebraically closed field and a description of the Galois group of the field extension generated by the fiber points.
skills.postconditions: A classification of the number of rational components of the fiber according to the orbits of the Galois action.
skills.example: For the map \(x\mapsto x^3\) over \(\mathbb{Q}\), the fiber over a rational value consists of three points forming a single Galois orbit unless the value is a cube, reflecting the splitting behavior of the cubic extension.

skills.name: perform_smoothness_check_via_jacobian_criterion
skills.description: Verify that a scheme defined by polynomial equations is smooth at a point by checking that the Jacobian matrix has maximal rank there.
skills.preconditions: A scheme given locally by explicit equations in an affine or projective space and a point at which smoothness is to be tested.
skills.postconditions: A conclusion that the point is smooth (if the rank condition holds) or singular (otherwise).
skills.example: The affine curve defined by \(y^2 - x^3 - x\) is smooth at the origin because the gradient \((\partial f/\partial x,\partial f/\partial y) = (-3x^2-1, 2y)\) evaluates to \((-1,0)\), which has full rank.

skills.name: apply_bezout_to_tangent_conditions
skills.description: Count the number of solutions to a system of tangency equations by interpreting each condition as a hypersurface and applying Bézout’s theorem to their intersection.
skills.preconditions: A collection of homogeneous polynomial equations each defining a hypersurface in a projective space, with the hypersurfaces meeting properly.
skills.postconditions: An upper bound (often exact in generic situations) for the number of common solutions given by the product of the degrees of the hypersurfaces.
skills.example: The set of lines tangent to a fixed smooth conic in the plane corresponds to solutions of a quadratic equation in the dual projective plane; Bézout predicts at most two such lines, and indeed there are exactly two.

skills.name: take_asymptotic_limit_of_average_counts
skills.description: Derive the limiting value of the average number of rational points in fibers of a family as the size of the base field tends to infinity, using the fact that the average converges to the generic fiber size.
skills.preconditions: A family of finite morphisms defined over \(\mathbb{F}_q\) with uniformly bounded degree and a notion of averaging over all \(\mathbb{F}_q\)-points of the base where the morphism is étale.
skills.postconditions: The limit of the average fiber cardinality as \(q\to\infty\) exists and equals the degree of the morphism.
skills.example: For the family of quadratic polynomials \(x^2 - t\) over \(\mathbb{F}_q\) with parameter \(t\), the average number of solutions in the étale locus approaches two as \(q\) grows, matching the degree two of the map.
